findings.desc: quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/tasks/capability-release-backfill-smoke.ts:302 declares `const capLedgerPathB = capabilityReleaseLedgerPath(rootB);` but never reads capLedgerPathB anywhere else in the file (confirmed via `tsc --noUnusedLocals`: TS6133). Dead local left over from CASE A's analogous ledgerPath/ledgerBefore pattern that was not carried through for CASE B.

quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/core/config.ts:226 the pre-existing capability_release_* global-phase wildcard is commented as read-only non-runtime product capability release provenance inspection and previously only matched the two read-only commands capability_release_list/capability_release_status. The new capability_release_backfill handler (packages/main/src/handlers/capability-release-backfill.ts) - a mainSharedMutating writer that git-commits ledger records and enriches playbook lineage under a learning-store lock - also matches this prefix and is silently granted allowedPhases:all through it (verified: isCommandAllowed(capability_release_backfill, phase) returns true for every phase via this wildcard, not via a dedicated entry). Every other allowedPhases:all mainSharedMutating command in this file (e.g. signature_backfill line 284, learning_scan line 290) gets its own explicit comment stating the phase-scope rationale per the files established convention; this new writer instead free-rides on a wildcard whose adjacent comment is now stale/inaccurate (no longer purely read-only inspection). Not a functional block (command works as intended), but an audit-trail/maintainability gap: a future reader auditing config.ts * -phase writers by comment would miss this one.
